title: Geometric Derivation of the Law of Sines
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: In any triangle ABC with sides a, b, c opposite angles A, B, C, let h be the length of the perpendicular altitude dropped from vertex A to the line containing side BC (of length a), considering both the case where angle C is acute and the case where angle C is obtuse (using \sin(\pi - \theta) = \sin\theta). Derive the Law of Sines: \frac{\sin A}{a} = \frac{\sin B}{b} = \frac{\sin C}{c}.

steps.title: Express Altitude h in Terms of Side c and Angle B
steps.explanation: Let D be the foot of the perpendicular from vertex A to line BC. In right triangle ABD, the side opposite angle B is h and the hypotenuse is AB = c, so h = c*sin B.
steps.why: In a right triangle, the sine of an acute angle is the ratio of the opposite leg to the hypotenuse.

steps.title: Express Altitude h in Terms of Side b and Angle C (Acute and Obtuse Cases)
steps.mathExpression: h = \begin{cases} b\sin C, & C \text{ acute} \\ b\sin(\pi - C) = b\sin C, & C \text{ obtuse} \end{cases}
steps.explanation: In right triangle ACD, the hypotenuse is AC = b. If C is acute, sin C = h/b directly. If C is obtuse, the interior angle of right triangle ACD at C is pi - C, so h = b*sin(pi - C) = b*sin C by the supplementary angle identity.
steps.why: By the sine difference formula, sin(pi - C) = sin pi cos C - cos pi sin C = sin C.

steps.title: Equate the Two Expressions for h and Extend to All Three Sides
steps.mathExpression: c\sin B = b\sin C \implies \frac{\sin B}{b} = \frac{\sin C}{c}; \quad \text{similarly } \frac{\sin A}{a} = \frac{\sin C}{c}
steps.explanation: Equating h = c*sin B and h = b*sin C and dividing by bc yields (sin B)/b = (sin C)/c. Repeating the construction with the altitude from vertex B to side AC gives (sin A)/a = (sin C)/c, completing the proof.
steps.why: Transitivity of equality combines the two proportions into the full Law of Sines.
